features.name: AGY stack_with_default: AGY ignores it at the top level and drops a false value; setup-host keeps a foreign statusLine
features.description: A live probe showed AGY reads stack_with_default only inside the statusLine object; the installer and setup-host.sh wrote it at the top level, where AGY ignores it, so the 'stop stacking' part of feat-068 changed nothing. Write it as false inside statusLine, remove the inert top-level key we wrote, correct the feat-068 evidence, and stop setup-host.sh from replacing a foreign AGY statusLine.
acceptance_criteria: install_statusline for gemini leaves stack_with_default out of settings.json on a fresh file, on a jq merge, on the refresh of our own script, and on the python fallback, and removes the top-level and the nested key if present
no other key in settings.json changes, and a foreign statusLine stays untouched by install_statusline and by setup-host.sh
a live agy session with the installed settings shows only our line (no native '? for shortcuts' line)
the feat-068 evidence no longer claims the installer turned stacking off
all 11 harness gates pass, with gate output saved to a file
features.evidence: Live probes in agy under tmux (160 cols): top-level stack_with_default true shows only our line; nested statusLine.stack_with_default true shows AGY's native line ('? for shortcuts', model) above ours; neither shows only ours. So the key must sit inside statusLine, and feat-068's top-level write never did anything. A first attempt wrote nested false; the installed file was clean right after install.sh but agy rewrote settings.json within about 20 s of a running session and removed the false (omitempty). The installer therefore writes no key at all, which is what 'off' means to AGY, and removes both the top-level and a nested true. scripts/tests/test_statusline_command.sh 38 passed (failed first: 4, then 5 after the rule changed): fresh, jq merge, refresh, old top-level true, nested true, python fallback without jq, foreign AGY statusLine left alone by install_statusline and by setup-host.sh (run against a throwaway HOME with closed stdin; the first version of that test hung on setup-host's ntfy prompt and was killed, real settings untouched). setup-host.sh now skips an AGY settings.json whose statusLine is not ours. harness-verify.sh passed all 11 gates with output saved to a file. feat-068's evidence carries a correction. Not done: no outside-model review (install-script change, one codex-kiro pass was run on feat-068 and its findings drove this); before the first message agy sends a payload the script shows only the left part of the line (unverified why, probably no context_window_size yet); the cause of the row sometimes sitting higher is still unknown and not reproduced; the Claude-side install paths are unchanged.

features.name: AGY statusline: show the 5-hour limit of the current model's family, not the lowest across families
features.description: The statusline showed the lowest *-5h bucket in agy's payload. agy keeps two separate 5-hour limits (Gemini models and Claude/GPT models, the payload's 3p-5h), so on a Gemini session with 59% left it showed '5h 0%' whenever the Claude/GPT limit was used up. Pick the bucket by model family and fall back to the lowest only when that bucket is missing.
acceptance_criteria: a model name starting with 'Gemini' shows the gemini-5h remaining percentage even when 3p-5h is lower

a model name starting with 'Claude' or 'GPT' shows the 3p-5h remaining percentage even when gemini-5h is lower; a name that is none of Gemini, Claude or GPT shows the lowest *-5h bucket, because the 3p mapping is not confirmed for other names
if the chosen bucket is missing, or the model name is empty, the lowest *-5h bucket is shown as before
a payload without quota (Claude Code) still renders cwd and context, and a malformed quota never blanks the line
the width, EOF and Claude Code cases in test_statusline_command.sh still pass
all 11 harness gates pass, with gate output saved to a file
features.evidence: Found by capturing every statusline call in live agy: the line showed '5h 0%' on a Gemini session that agy's own /quota reported at 59% five-hour remaining, because the script took the lowest *-5h bucket and agy keeps a separate Claude/GPT limit (payload 3p-5h) that was used up; it had looked right earlier only because 3p-5h happened to be full. The line now shows the model family's own bucket (Gemini -> gemini-5h, Claude/GPT -> 3p-5h, any other name or missing bucket -> lowest). After install, live agy showed 5h 57% while agy -p /quota showed Gemini five-hour remaining 57%; run time 65 ms. scripts/test_statusline_command.sh 49 passed (failed first: 4, then 4 after the review). A fresh subagent found remaining_fraction was not range-checked (-0.5 printed '5h -50%', 1.5 printed '5h 150%', and an out-of-range own bucket hid a valid fallback) and, as a pre-existing case, a non-object model blanked the whole line; both fixed with failing tests first. harness-verify.sh passed all 11 gates with output saved to a file. Also learned: before the first message agy's first payloads have agent_state authenticating, context_window_size 0 and no quota, so the line shows only [model] cwd git:(branch) for about 4 s (12 s once, cause not found); the script takes 60-90 ms per call and is not the cause. Not done: the 3p-5h mapping for Claude and GPT names is a guess, since agy -p /model lists only the current model and no Claude or GPT display name was seen; the model's own weekly limit (agy shows 'Gemini 4 Argon Weekly Limit 0%') is not displayed; the 12 s startup case and the occasional higher row are unexplained.

features.name: Runtime drift gate also checks the installed statusline scripts
features.description: After the last edit of config/statusline-command.sh the installed AGY copy was never refreshed, so the live line ran an older version until a later review noticed. The runtime-drift gate compared only the flat runtime copies. Make it also compare each installed statusline-command.sh (AGY and Claude) with config/statusline-command.sh, but only when that agent's settings.json points at our copy, so a foreign statusLine is never flagged.
acceptance_criteria: the gate blocks (exit 2) and names the file when an installed statusline-command.sh that settings.json names exactly (statusLine.command == 'bash <copy>', and the path appears literally in the file) differs from config/statusline-command.sh or is missing, for an agent in the saved selection (none saved means claude), in a main checkout with jq available

the gate passes when the copy matches, with a foreign or non-object statusLine, our path in another key, a longer path, a tilde form, absent, truncated or non-object settings.json, an agent outside the saved selection, a linked worktree, a non-default branch, a repo without config/statusline-command.sh, or an unset HOME
the existing runtime-copy checks and their tests are unchanged, and an absent runtime dir is still a SKIP for that part only
gate_experiment.py still reports the runtime drift gate as catching its planted defect, and the clean baseline still passes
a fresh subagent and a different model family review the change (it is a gate)
all 11 harness gates pass, with gate output saved to a file
features.evidence: Incident: after config/statusline-command.sh changed, the installed AGY copy ran an older script until a later review noticed. The gate now also compares each installed statusline-command.sh with config/statusline-command.sh. harness/guards/tests/test_runtime_drift_guard.sh 43 passed (22 first; failed first: 6, then 9 after the first review, then 2 after the second). Built in a fake repo on main so the result does not depend on the branch or worktree. Two reviews (fresh subagent, codex-kiro) of the first version found the gate would block on things bash scripts/install.sh cannot clear, which would keep a Stop hook blocking the agent: linked worktree or non-default branch (install.sh refuses), an agent outside the saved selection, a missing repo source file, a substring match that took our path in another key or a .sh.bak path or truncated JSON as ours, and the tilde form; all reproduced and fixed with tests first. A re-review (fresh subagent and codex-kiro) found two more: no saved selection means a bare non-interactive install.sh selects claude only (confirmed), and a HOME that JSON escapes (wire_hook writes \u00e9) is found by jq but not by install_statusline's literal grep, so the block could never clear (confirmed with the real functions); both fixed with tests first. Four mutations of the final guard (literal grep, no-selection default, selection check, worktree check) are each caught. Real machine: guard exit 0. Throwaway HOME built by the real install.sh: clean install passes, a stale copy blocks naming the file, and the hinted bash scripts/install.sh clears it. scripts/gate_experiment.py --case runtime-drift-lib-edit: the planted drift is still caught and runtime drift is rated needed. harness-verify.sh passed all 11 gates with output saved to a file, run alone. One earlier full-gate run failed scripts/tests/test_run_tests_parallel.sh (SIGTERM test, queue left=1) while a review and a gate experiment ran at the same time; solo it passed 3 of 3 and two concurrent copies passed 3 rounds of 3, so it is unattributed and may be a load flake (same family as the 94/1 seen in feat-068). Not done: with HOME unset and no RUNTIME_DRIFT_GUARD_RUNTIME_DIR the guard exits 1 at skills_runtime_dir (also true before this change; the test for unset HOME only covers the statusline part); a selection file with spaces or CRLF is not trimmed like install.sh trims it (only a hand-edited file); install.sh against a throwaway HOME runs a slow live agent probe.

features.name: Telemetry housekeeping: capped gate-runs log, named git failures, no tiny tail records
features.description: Three leftovers from the feat-070 review. (1) harness-verify-runs.jsonl grows by a line per gate run and is read whole for every record: cap it. (2) A completed feature in a repo where git fails or feature_list.json is untracked reports 'completion not committed', which names the wrong cause: report each cause. (3) Every session-clean.sh run writes a small run record for the seconds since the completion commit that no feature claims: skip a window with almost no activity, since the next record's window starts at the last recorded end and absorbs it.
acceptance_criteria: harness-verify.sh appends each run to harness-verify-runs-YYYYMM.jsonl (one short append, no lock, nothing rewritten) and deletes monthly files older than twelve months, leaves no temp file, and changes neither exit code nor console output; run_telemetry.py reads the old unsuffixed file and every monthly file beside it

feature_run_record.py reports 'completion not committed' only for a tracked feature_list.json whose completion no commit shows, 'feature_list.json is not tracked by git' when it is untracked, and a no-git status when the directory is not a repository or git is missing

session-clean.sh skips the run record and warns for every git status except 'not a git repository' (completion not committed, feature_list.json is not tracked by git, git cannot read this repository, git is not available, no work tree to read feature_list.json from)

run_telemetry.py --current-session --min-rows N writes nothing when the window has fewer than N usage rows, no subagent and no outside-agent attempt; a window with zero parent rows is skipped unless it has a subagent (an outside-agent attempt is machine-wide, so it does not count for that rule); without the flag nothing else changes; the next record's window starts at the last recorded end and counts the skipped rows
session-clean.sh passes --min-rows 10
a fresh subagent and a different model family review the change (it edits the gate runner and the session close)
all 11 harness gates pass, with gate output saved to a file, run with nothing else running
features.verification: python3 -m pytest tests/test_feature_run_record.py tests/test_run_telemetry.py -q && bash scripts/tests/test_harness_verify.sh && bash scripts/tests/test_session_clean.sh && bash scripts/harness-verify.sh
features.evidence: Measured first: of 39 run records, 29 were unclaimed and 21 of those had under 10 usage rows and no subagent or outside attempt; none of the 21 was claimed by a feature. --min-rows 10 skips only that kind. Tests first (each failed before the code): 202 pytest (tests/test_feature_run_record.py, tests/test_run_telemetry.py), test_harness_verify.sh 30, test_session_clean.sh 26. mypy clean. harness-verify.sh passed all 11 gates, run alone with nothing else running, output saved to a file. Reviews: three rounds, each a fresh subagent and codex-kiro. Round 1 found the first log cap lost a concurrently appended line (reproduced by forcing the interleaving), missing git crashed the recorder, a bare or unreadable repo was called 'not a git repository', session-clean did not pass --outside-log, and a window with zero parent rows but a subagent was dropped. Round 2 found the mkdir lock I added was unsound: a stale-lock takeover race, a killed holder blocking for up to two minutes (find -mmin +1 means stale after about 120 s, measured), ten-second stalls on an unwritable directory, and a lost line if the holder pauses. I dropped the lock instead of patching it a third time: the log is now one append-only file per month, so there is nothing to lock or rewrite, at the cost of retention by age (twelve months) instead of the newest 1000 lines. Round 3 found git commands inherit GIT_DIR and GIT_WORK_TREE and could read another repository (reproduced), another session's outside-agent attempt could force a record for an idle window (the log is machine-wide), and a directory named like a monthly file reported 'measured, 0 runs' instead of missing; all fixed with a failing test first. A race test that I first ran against a broken mutation died before its first assertion and proved nothing; the valid mutation (lock removed) failed the race test as it should. Not fixed: a legacy row copied into a monthly file would be counted twice (rows have no run id; nothing here copies rows); monthly retention keeps 13 files in January; git's 'not a git repository' is told from an unreadable repo by finding a .git entry in the directory or a parent, so a plain directory under a stray parent .git reads as unreadable (it skips the run record, which is the safe side); GNU find and bash 3.2 were not run for the new code beyond the existing portability gate. One earlier full-gate run failed test_run_tests_parallel.sh while a review and a gate experiment ran at the same time; solo it passed 9 of 9 runs, so it is recorded as an unattributed load flake.
